prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies transformer/feeder bays; approved designs/limits govern equipment, protection, wiring.
Elements/items: Bay Automation Controller (Juniper), North Bay Controller, South Bay Controller automate bays; Juniper evaluates status/permissives, produces Bay Status Digest. Breaker Control Unit executes authorized operations, enforces interlocks. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) protects assigned feeder independently of supervision; produces Relay Diagnostic Note. Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing) consolidates indications/communications quality; produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip; replaces neither local indications nor protection. Station Gateway carries authorized external supervisory communications. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) distributes satellite-derived network time; produces Clock Drift Snapshot at configured offset condition. Sequence Event Archive retains events. Engineering Workstation revision-controls working/approved configurations/history; produces Settings Review Receipt upon review completion; access restricted to assigned engineering personnel. Maintenance Remote Terminal provides approved maintenance access, not local authority. Station DC System powers automation/protection; loss interrupts visibility/timing.
Actors: Control Room Operator assesses displays, verifies commanded states, coordinates energized-equipment work access with Switching Desk Coordinator. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) develops/documents changes. Substation Field Crew (Cinder) inspects, maintains, supports switching under authorized instructions/clearances; confirms work authorization/site-entry controls before access. Substation Supervisor enforces change authorization/operational controls, escalates availability concerns.
Requirements: Local selection/interlocks prevail; remote commands require authority, bay selection, permissions, availability. Control failure must not inhibit trips. Communications loss yields stale/unavailable displays; verify currency after recovery. Timing supports correlation, not protection validity; reference loss invokes device-specific clocks/holdover; indicate synchronized/degraded/unavailable quality.
Settings define pickup/delay/logic. Changes require study/current-equipment basis, documented effects, unique prereview revision, coordination verification including upstream/downstream operating range, independent qualified review of calculations/logic/applicability, completeness/consistency/suitability; copied values alone insufficient. Record approval before release; verify model/firmware compatibility. Protection-affecting deployment requires approved outage/window. Compare installed/approved values; functionally check relay; discrepancies block release pending resolution/review.

New part:
S078: The Substation Supervisor confirms that the requested work is consistent with current operating conditions and approved procedures.
S079: The crew reviews the work scope, access route, known hazards, and communication arrangements before entering the yard.
S080: Personnel use the site access process to record arrival and departure so that the control room can account for field staff.
S081: Work boundaries are established before tools or test equipment are brought near electrical apparatus.
S082: The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms the applicable switching and clearance arrangements before work begins.
S083: The Control Room Operator retains authority to suspend work when operating conditions change or indications become uncertain.
S084: The Substation Field Crew verifies equipment identity at the point of work against the approved work documentation.
S085: Field personnel do not rely on screen indications alone to establish that equipment is safe to approach or handle.
S086: Required checks of position, isolation, and absence of hazardous energy are performed using approved site procedures.
S087: Any discrepancy between field observations and control-room indications is treated as an unsafe condition until resolved.
S088: The crew promptly reports uncertain equipment conditions through the designated operational communication channel.
S089: Substation Field Crew completes and sends the Breaker Inspection Tag after recording the observed breaker condition and inspection time.
S090: The Station Supervisory Control System presents available equipment indications for operator review during normal operation.
S091: The Bay Automation Controller applies configured permissives and interlocks to supported automated operations.
S092: Automation does not replace field verification when a procedure requires direct confirmation of equipment condition.
S093: The Control Room Operator evaluates reported field conditions before authorizing a return to automated operation.
S094: Field crews maintain communications with the control room throughout work that could affect protection, control, or service continuity.
S095: If communications are lost, the crew stops affected work and follows the approved hold and escalation procedure.
S096: Work is considered complete only after personnel, tools, and temporary connections are accounted for and the work area is left in a safe state.
S097: The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms the operational handback arrangements before equipment is returned to service.
S098: The Sequence Event Archive is the station's authoritative repository for time-stamped operational event evidence.
S099: The Sequence Event Archive is known operationally as Orchard.
S100: It preserves event records in their received form so later review does not depend on transient operator displays.
S101: Each retained record includes its source identity, event time, archive receipt time, and available quality indications.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
